Can an Independent Appraisal Help Lower Your Property Taxes?

When your county’s estimate seems too high, it is tempting to assume a private appraisal will lower your tax bill.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

THE SHORT ANSWER

Before ordering an appraisal solely for an appeal, review the notice, identify the specific issue, and confirm the filing deadline and evidence requirements with the Pima County Assessor. Reddy Appraisal LLC offers independent residential valuation services that can help homeowners understand their property’s market position.

Identify the issue behind the appeal

When your county’s estimate seems too high, it is tempting to assume a private appraisal will lower your tax bill. The reality is more nuanced. In Pima County, an assessment appeal is intended to challenge an improper valuation, an incorrect property description or classification, or an incorrectly calculated limited property value—not simply to protest a tax increase. A professional appraisal may be valuable evidence when the disputed issue involves full cash value.

Match the analysis to the effective date

An appraiser examines relevant sales, property condition, location, size, and other factors to develop a supported opinion of market value as of a specified date. That can be especially helpful for homes with unusual layouts, deferred maintenance, adverse location influences, or features that are not accurately represented in county records. The effective date matters: an appraisal prepared for today may not answer a valuation question tied to an earlier statutory date.

Confirm the process and evidence requirements

Before ordering an appraisal solely for an appeal, review the notice, identify the specific issue, and confirm the filing deadline and evidence requirements with the Pima County Assessor. Reddy Appraisal LLC offers independent residential valuation services that can help homeowners understand their property’s market position. The assessor or appeals authority makes the final decision, and a successful challenge does not guarantee a particular tax savings amount.
